newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota launches new luxury models in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Toyota launches new luxury models in Japan.

text.p: Japanese car giant Toyota Motor Corp launched three completely remodelled luxury sedans in Japan on Thursday, hoping to lift its share of the domestic market.
Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda told Reuters the new Mark II, Chaser and Cresta models had monthly sales targets of 12,500, 5,000 and 6,000 units respectively.

Asked if Toyota would achieve its targeted 40 percent share in the domestic market this year, Okuda replied: "I am sure we can achieve the target as we will introduce some other new models...later this year."
Toyota's domestic market share, excluding 660cc minivehicles, stood at 38.8 percent in the January to August period this year, down from 39.6 percent in the same period last year.
Slower domestic sales were due to sluggish demand for Toyota's current saloon models and a delay in its introduction of several new multi-purpose vehicles.

In contrast, Honda Motor Co managed a domestic share of 9.4 percent in January to August, up from 7.2 percent the year before, helped by launches of new recreational vehicle series like the Odyssey, CR-V and Step Wagon.

Toyota said all models in the Mark II series have a newly developed engine combining power with fuel economy, dual airbags, front-seat side airbags, and an anti-lock braking system. A traction control system is either standard or optional depending on the model and a vehicle stability control system is standard on 3-litre versions.
The domestic selling price for the new Mark II starts at 2.25 million yen ($20,600).
"Slow January to August domestic sales were due to the fact that the domestic economy did not grow as much as we expected but our sales will rise from September," Okuda said.

"We see no quick recovery in the domestic market in view of uncertainties such as the economy of the United States and the falling (domestic) stock market, but we will not revise our forecast of overall vehicle demand," he said.

He said the company's forecast of Japan's overall vehicle demand was 5.40 million units in calendar 1996. He said Toyota sales would account for 2.18 million of this total after the launch of more new models later this year.
Toyota's domestic sales in the first eight months of this calendar year totalled 1.35 million units, down 0.8 percent from a year earlier.
Nikko Research Center has said it expects Toyota's parent current profit to rise to 530 billion yen ($4.86 billion) this business year helped by new models and a stable yen against the dollar.
In May, Toyota forecast parent current profit of 480 billion yen ($4.40 billion) in 1996/97, up 40.9 percent from 340.7 billion yen ($3.12 billion) the year before. ($1=109)
